facts.text: The Bloody Baron's storyline, regardless of its ending, ends with him confronting the ruin of his own life.
The Baron's tale functions as a warning to Geralt about how personal failings can destroy a father-daughter bond.
Geralt's time in Velen prepares him emotionally for his eventual reunion with Ciri.
Novigrad was once known as a free city and a center of trade and intellectual life before falling under religious persecution.
The Church of the Eternal Fire, led by Caleb Menge and the Temple Guard, carried out violent persecution of mages and nonhumans in Novigrad.
Suspected mages and nonhumans were burned publicly in Novigrad's Hierarch Square.
Geralt travels to Novigrad searching for Dandelion, the last person known to have seen Ciri in the city.
Novigrad's underworld was controlled by four crime lords: Sigi Reuven, Sigismund Dijkstra, and the King of Beggars among them.
Geralt performs tasks for the Novigrad crime lords while searching for information about Dandelion and Ciri.
Geralt discovers that Dandelion and Ciri had attempted to rob Dijkstra's vault to fund a way to break a curse affecting Avallac'h.
Geralt helps Triss Merigold organize a mass escape of mages and alchemists through Novigrad's sewers.
As a mutant, Geralt becomes a target of the anti-mage, anti-nonhuman bigotry sweeping Novigrad.
Geralt rescues Dandelion after a series of dangerous schemes, including staging a play and a prison break.
Dandelion tells Geralt that Ciri escaped the Temple Guard in Novigrad by teleporting away, going into hiding once more.
After Novigrad, Geralt heads to the Skellige Isles, believing it to be one of the few places the Eternal Fire's influence has not reached.
In Skellige, Geralt reunites with his old friend Crach an Craite, who had looked after Ciri during her childhood summers.
Skellige is undergoing a succession crisis following the death of King Bran.
Geralt helps Crach an Craite's children, Hjalmar and Cerys, in their quests connected to the succession crisis.
Geralt investigates the site of a massive magical explosion on the island of Ard Skellig, caused by a battle between Ciri, Avallac'h, and the Wild Hunt.
Geralt and Yennefer use the Mask of Uroboros to witness magical echoes of the past on Ard Skellig.
The vision reveals that Ciri's elder blood power leveled entire forests during the confrontation with the Wild Hunt.
The Wild Hunt's spectral riders attack the village of Undvik, leaving it in ruins and its people haunted.
Geralt becomes involved in choosing Skellige's next ruler, deciding between Hjalmar and Cerys.
The people of Skellige, especially Crach an Craite, consider Ciri family and offer help without political motive, unlike the Emperor of Nilfgaard.
Skellige is portrayed as the only place where Ciri is seen as a person rather than a prophecy.
Geralt discovers a creature called Uma, found on Skellige's shores after the magical explosion, who carries a curse masking his true identity.
Geralt realizes Uma is the key to finding Ciri and travels to Kaer Morhen to attempt to break the curse.
Lifting Uma's curse reveals that the creature is actually the elven sage Avallac'h.
Following this revelation, Geralt sails to the Isle of Mists to find Ciri.
On the Isle of Mists, Geralt finds Ciri in a catatonic state, her soul seemingly lost after her last interdimensional jump.
Ciri is revived through the residual magic of the Wisp/Will-o'-the-Wisp, waking to see Geralt.
After being found, Ciri describes the Wild Hunt as a constant, physical pressure that pursued her across every world she visited.
Ciri's relationship with Geralt shifts from ward and mentor to equal partners preparing to face the Wild Hunt together.
Geralt and Ciri leave the Isle of Mists together to return to the continent and confront the Wild Hunt.
Geralt and Ciri travel to Kaer Morhen to prepare for a final stand against the Wild Hunt.
At Kaer Morhen, Geralt gathers allies including Yennefer, Triss Merigold, fellow Witchers Eskel and Lambert, and friends Roach and Letho.
The defenders at Kaer Morhen prepare potions and magical traps ahead of the Wild Hunt's assault.
The Battle of Kaer Morhen is fought against the Wild Hunt, who arrive amid a magical frost storm with spectral ships.
During the Battle of Kaer Morhen, Vesemir sacrifices his life protecting Ciri from Eredin's general Imlerith.
Vesemir's death triggers an uncontrolled eruption of Ciri's elder blood power, forcing the Wild Hunt to retreat.
Geralt considers Vesemir's death the loss of his true father figure and the end of the era of the old Witchers.
Vesemir's body is cremated on a pyre near Kaer Morhen after the battle.
After Vesemir's death, Ciri resolves to end Eredin's pursuit for good, displaying a hardened resolve reminiscent of her grandmother Calanthe.
Following the battle, Geralt's coalition retrieves the Sunstone and allies with the Lodge of Sorceresses to lure Eredin into a trap.
The final battle against the Wild Hunt takes place on the shores of Undvik in the Skellige Isles.
Geralt leads a coalition of Skellige warriors, Nilfgaardian soldiers, and the Lodge of Sorceresses to draw out the Wild Hunt using the Sunstone.
Geralt duels Eredin Bréacc Glas, king of the Wild Hunt, aboard a dying ship during the battle.
Eredin fights with cold precision and world-jumping abilities, while Geralt fights with desperation using every sign and oil available to him.
As Geralt kills him, Eredin reveals with his final words that Avallac'h has taken Ciri and deceived them both.
Geralt finds Avallac'h at the center of a magical storm and learns he is not a traitor but a facilitator of Ciri's plan.
Ciri chooses to enter the White Frost herself to use her elder blood power to stop the encroaching entropy of the multiverse.
Geralt is forced to let Ciri face the White Frost alone, trusting she is strong enough to survive without him.
Ciri's victory over the White Frost destroys the Wild Hunt and saves the continent from being frozen.
Geralt of Rivia's story concludes with one of three possible fates for Ciri, depending on the player's choices.
In the Witcher ending, Ciri fakes her death to escape her destiny and Geralt gives her a custom silver sword at an inn in White Orchard, welcoming her as a fellow Witcher.
In the Empress ending, Ciri decides to travel to Nilfgaard and take the throne as the Emperor's successor to bring peace to the continent, parting from Geralt at White Orchard.
In the death ending, Ciri fails to return from the White Frost if Geralt did not provide her enough emotional support and autonomy, leaving Geralt broken.
In the death ending, Geralt returns to Velen to hunt the last remaining crone and recover Ciri's lost medallion, ultimately dying in the swamp.
After the main story, Geralt may retire to the vineyard of Corvo Bianco in Toussaint, finding peace with either Yennefer or Triss.
